design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (rental_reimbursement_claims, category rental) — round 2

[Step 0 draw] scripts/draw_counts.py --task 0 -> prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[4,4,5,5]. Assignment (round 2): rental_ext_upgrade_acceptance_days 4, rental_ext_partner_invoice_settlement 4, rental_ext_rideshare_day_allowance 5, rental_ext_extension_day_room 5 (root).

[Why this is a good test] The customer asks one thing: extend the rental while backordered parts come in. The number of days is a day-room figure that exists only once three other problems are resolved, each stated in the extension rule as a prerequisite sentence over a record-visible state: the SUV she has driven since 2026-09-15 has no authorization (her own acceptance of the larger class records it); the closed partner rental of August has no agency payment; the closed rideshare authorization has no reimbursement. Each changes the extension (3 with all three; 0 / 5 / 5 when one is skipped). Every computation is multi-factor over the claim's ledger (authorized vs billed days, close reasons, parts-delay extensions, closing end dates), the physical damage claim file (drivable flag, report date, supplement amount and shop type), roadside events (accident tow moved to the claim, trip-interruption alternate transportation) and the auto package's rental rank. Tools are plain writes.

[Scope] This task claims rental_ext_extension_day_room, rental_ext_upgrade_acceptance_days, rental_ext_partner_invoice_settlement, rental_ext_rideshare_day_allowance and tools extend_rental_authorization_97458fea (agent), accept_upgraded_rental_aa4639f2 (user), pay_partner_rental_invoice_bf34992c (agent), submit_rideshare_receipts_3a988a26 (user). Task 1 holds the overbilling credit and the customer-arranged-rental reimbursement on other events and tools.

[Problem-tree card] root rental_ext_extension_day_room (rental_extension.authorized_days, on_request, agent).
edge 1 -> rental_ext_upgrade_acceptance_days, value_input, gate run_days, form state: 'The days an extension adds are fixed only after the rental it extends stands on the rental ledger as an authorization under the claim.' Only the larger-class acceptance writes authorization entries. Seed: latest authorization entered is RA-26-0819-55206 (closed, end date 2026-09-10); none starts 2026-09-15. Owner user.
edge 2 -> rental_ext_partner_invoice_settlement, value_input, gate car_billed, form state: 'The days an extension adds are not settled until every closed partner direct-bill rental on the claim carries an agency payment on the rental ledger.' (negated). Only the agency payment tool writes agency payments. Seed: RA-26-0819-55206 closed; the option's only agency payment is on PD-2024-0533187.
edge 3 -> rental_ext_rideshare_day_allowance, value_input, gate ride_days_billed, form state: 'Before the days an extension adds are worked out, every closed rideshare, taxi or transit authorization on the claim must carry a reimbursement entry on the rental ledger.' Only the rideshare submission writes rideshare reimbursements. Seed: RA-26-0818-20417 closed (end date 2026-08-19), no reimbursement. Owner user.
Topological order used: payment (11), rideshare (13), acceptance (15), extension (17); the three prerequisites commute (harness run with the reverse order: identical terminal DB; 779.22 / 57.00 / 5 in both). Deletion runs: skip acceptance -> 0, skip payment -> 5, skip rideshare -> 5; gold 3. user_scenario names none of the three; tools validate nothing.

[Base-invariant card] rental_extension: within_max_days and the increment/cap sentence are declared overwritten (day room with comeback addition, package days and counted days). rental_authorization (acceptance): claim_accepted_for_rental (decision accepted 2026-08-18), option_active_for_rental (active), theft_waiting_period (collision, not a theft; boundaries in temporal_feasibility); the first-authorization day sentence is overwritten by 'The authorized days are the repair days plus the package days ...'. rental_vendor_payment: once-only invoice gate restated; BRC-0910-447182 not on the ledger. rental_reimbursement_payment: receipts_in_time, end date 2026-08-19 day 0, 2026-09-22 day 34 (in time), day 60 = 2026-10-18.

[Business-object card] Claim PD-2026-0871405 on the CR-V's 60/1800 option. Agency payment: RA-26-0819-55206 (3 extensions, closing for completed repairs). Rideshare: RA-26-0818-20417. Extension: the authorization returned by the acceptance. Excluded: 2024 claim PD-2024-0533187 rows; the Camry's 30/900 option.

[Factor card] (harness figures; result -> each factor's baseline figure)
agency payment 779.22 (all baselines 906.40): invoiced_closing_allowance 1 grace day (closed for completed repairs) -> 739.26; partner_rate_convention weekly 20 of 23 -> 899.10; partner_program_share 0.97 -> 803.40; parts_delay_day_share 0.95 on 10 days -> 799.20. Near-miss: the invoice's 24th day (car dropped back 2026-09-11) lies past the closing end date and is the customer's.
rideshare 57.00 (all baselines 120.00): first covered day 2026-08-17 -> 9.50; last covered day 2026-08-18 (partner car entered on the end date of the rideshare closing) -> 74.50; allowance 45.00 -> 82.00; package top-up +2.50 -> 52.00; trip set-off 38.00 -> 95.00. Near-miss: authorization keyed with start 2026-08-18; receipts cover three days.
acceptance 5 (all baselines 7): repair_path_starting_days 2 -> 10; recalibration_days_owed 1 -> 4; recalibration_scheduling (non-network sublet: 2 + 1 + 1) -> 4; package_rental_days 1 -> 4.
extension 3 (all baselines 0): comeback_day_maximum_addition +2 -> 1; agency_days_counted 23 -> 2; rideshare_day_weight 2 -> 2; package_day_room_addition +1 -> 2; agency_rental_closing_allowance 1 -> 4.
Multi-source: repair_path_starting_days, comeback_day_maximum_addition, partner_program_share, rideshare_first_covered_day. Cross-difficulty: physdmg, roadside, auto. No stamp field decides a tier.

[Seed rows] customer/policy/vehicles; physdmg coverage and claim events (report not drivable, accepted, estimate 0 and supplement 1 at a non-network shop); roadside option and events (allowance grant, 2026-08-17 accident tow and its restore, alternate transportation 38.00); rental options and ledger. Round 2 removed the 2026-09-14 tow (no factor reads tow mileage any more) and set the roadside calls remaining to 4.

[Persona] Hurried nurse; opening is the extension request only; identity, rental details, closing receipt (24 days at 41.20) and rides only on request; runs the two customer tools only when handed over; ends only after the representative confirms the extension is recorded and gives its days.

[Standard solution] locate -> verify (6145550164, 7742) -> read policy, vehicles, rental options, ledger, physdmg coverages, claim events, roadside option and events -> pay BRC-0910-447182 (24 days, 41.20): 779.22 -> customer submits RS-PRUITT-0817-0819, 3 days, 57.00 -> customer accepts standard_suv, 2026-09-15, 74.90, 5 days (returns the new authorization) -> extend it, sequence 1, 3 days, parts_delay.

[Draft recomputation from visible context] From published rules, ledger, claim file, roadside events and the customer's lines, the figures above are reproduced. Easy mistakes: counting 24 or 22 agency days, ignoring the grace day, counting 3 rideshare days, using the closing's entry date instead of its end date, extending the closed August rental.

[Round 2 revisions — audit items]
F1: the acceptance rule now states the default only as 'Under the standard method ...'; the declared override (replaced_by) is the factor-driven total 'The authorized days are the repair days plus the package days ...'. One unconditional statement of authorized days remains.
F2: the last-day tier of the rideshare rule reads 'entered on the end date of the rideshare authorization's closing' (the closing's end_date, as computed); the closing's entry date plays no role.
F3: recalibration_shop_conversion (multiplier) removed; replaced by recalibration_scheduling, a method choosing concurrent (larger of), sublet-sequential (sum plus transfer day) or sequential (sum) scheduling.
F4: both tow-mileage factors removed (acceptance and extension); the 2026-09-14 tow row removed.
F5: household_package_share removed from the agency payment.
F6: invoiced_covered_days with its unreachable tier removed; covered days are the closed span capped at authorized days plus a closing allowance chosen by close reason (repairs complete -> repair_complete_grace_days, total-loss offer -> total_loss_rental_end_days, otherwise none), the base end rules.
Counts: acceptance 4, agency payment 4, rideshare 5 (new package top-up), extension 5 (new package day-room addition and agency rental closing allowance) = draw [4,4,5,5].
Observations handled: persona now closes only after the extension is confirmed recorded; invoice reads 24 days.

[Round 3 revision — audit item N1] The partner-invoice rule stated two unconditional caps on covered days ('never more than its authorized days' and 'never more than the authorized days plus the closing allowance'). The first is now the standard method only ('Under the standard method the covered days of a partner invoice are the closed span ..., never more than its authorized days'), and the allowance sentence says it applies 'in place of the standard cap at the authorized days'. On this world one reading remains: covered min(23, 22 + 1) = 23, billable 20, amount 779.22; the 739.26 reading is the baseline figure of invoiced_closing_allowance, not a second answer. No value, world row or persona line changed.
user_scenario: You are Marisol Pruitt, a pediatric nurse in Columbus, Ohio, calling Cardinal Mutual on a short break between patients, so you are friendly but a little hurried and you like plain answers. Your 2023 Honda CR-V was hit on August 17 on the way back from Cincinnati; it was repaired once, but it went back to the body shop on September 14 because they found more damage, and you have been driving a rental from the rental counter there since September 15. You open by saying the shop called this morning: the replacement parts for the hidden damage are backordered, so you need Cardinal to extend your rental so you can keep driving it while the parts come in, and you would like it done on this call rather than waiting for a callback. You are happy for the representative to take care of whatever Cardinal has to do on its side to make that happen. If the representative asks how to find you, you give your phone number, 6145550164. When they ask for something to verify you, you give the last four of your driver's license, 7742; only if they still need another detail you add your date of birth, 1984-03-19, or your ZIP code, 43214. You do not have the claim number handy and say it is the claim for the 2023 Honda CR-V. You only describe the current rental when the representative asks about it: you picked it up at the Buckeye Rent-A-Car counter at the shop, the agreement says pickup 2026-09-15, and it is a standard SUV because the counter had nothing smaller that day; the agreement shows a rate of $74.90 a day, and the counter told you that anything above what Cardinal pays would be yours, which is fine with you. You only bring up your first rental if the representative asks about it or about any paperwork from it: you returned that car when the CR-V was first fixed, and you still have the closing receipt Buckeye Rent-A-Car gave you, which shows invoice BRC-0910-447182, 24 days at $41.20 a day, billed to Cardinal, because you dropped that car back on September 11; you read those details out exactly as printed when asked. Likewise, only if the representative asks how you got around right after the accident do you explain that you took Lyft and Uber rides for the first few days until the rental counter had a car; you kept every receipt, your receipt summary is labeled RS-PRUITT-0817-0819, and the receipts cover three days, August 17, 18 and 19. You never added the fares up and say the representative will know better than you what Cardinal pays for them. When the representative explains that you have to submit those ride receipts yourself and hands the submission to you, you submit them with that receipt summary label, the three days, and exactly the amount the representative quotes, and you read back whatever confirmation comes up. When the representative explains that you have to accept the larger rental yourself and hands that acceptance to you, you accept it with the standard SUV, the 2026-09-15 pickup date, the $74.90 daily rate and exactly the number of days the representative tells you, and you read the new authorization number back if they ask. Once the representative confirms the extension is recorded on your rental and tells you how many days it adds, you accept that number as it is, say you understand that any days beyond it are yours to pay the counter, thank them and end the call. You do not know how Cardinal counts rental days or works out payments, and you never suggest numbers or steps of your own.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The count runs from the end_date of the closed authorization, that date being day 0, and receipts received on the last day are in time.

boundary_check.at_boundary: A submission on 2026-10-18 (day 60) is in time because the boundary is inclusive.

temporal_feasibility.condition: For a total theft, a rental may start no earlier than theft_waiting_days calendar days after the theft was reported.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The days count from the report_date on the theft claim, the report date being day 0, so with a waiting period of 1 the rental can start on the day after the report.

boundary_check.just_before: The loss is collision_vehicle, not a theft, so no waiting period applies; for a theft reported 2026-08-17 under this option (theft_waiting_days 0) a start on 2026-08-16 would precede the report and fail.
boundary_check.at_boundary: A theft start on 2026-08-17 (day 0, waiting 0) would be allowed; the 2026-09-15 pickup is 29 days after the report.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The three prerequisite writes commute: the agency payment reads only the closed partner rental and the per-loss room (1800.00 or 1743.00, never binding against 779.22); the rideshare reimbursement reads the rideshare authorization and the per-loss room (1800.00 or 1020.78, never binding against 57.00); the larger-class acceptance reads no payment at all. Harness runs with orders (payment, rideshare, acceptance) and (acceptance, rideshare, payment) give 779.22 / 57.00 / 5 and an extension of 3 in both, and identical terminal rows (row ids are content hashes of the arguments). The extension is last because its rule waits on all three states.
